what.summary: Operator opened with the same full-chunk delegation pattern the last four sessions ran under — 'Fire up and continue wherever the other guy left off and fill up your contacts till you're done. Find a good stopping point sounds delicious.' The prior letter named Phase E4 cut 3 as the recommended first move and explicitly pre-wrote the chip-form question about how wide to scope the cut. Carpenter surfaced the chip on session-start per PFOR-019 with four options (full cut 3 / just org-creation picker / just JoinOrgModal / picker+members skipping the modal); operator picked full cut 3. Cut 3 ships three interlocking threads in one commit: the JoinPolicyPicker as a sibling to OrgRulesEditor in the same SettingsScreen lazy-load pattern (six policy-kind sub-forms with per-kind validation mirroring buildAuthSubtree's contract; tracked as a separate state slot from org-action rules and folded into one AuthRule[] at submit time so buildAuthSubtree gets a canonical input); the OrgIdentitySections expansion with a Joined-members section pulling acceptedSelfMemberships in chronological order plus an amber-chip publish-roster button driven by pendingSelfMemberships; and the novel JoinOrgModal at src/features/connections/JoinOrgModal.tsx — the any-wallet join-an-org flow that takes a paste-or-scanned org self-declaration, parses + validates via parseEnvelope + isOrganizationSelfDeclaration, reads the join-policy via findAuthRule + isJoinRule, renders the policy in plain language via a kind-dispatched describePolicy helper, walks the joiner through picking a proof-eligible attestation when the policy is requires_handshake / requires_credential (the filter helpers findHandshakeProofCandidates + findCredentialProofCandidates inline in the modal), calls tapit-attest's disclosureProof on the chosen leaf (verification for handshake, credential_type for credential), bakes the bundle into buildSelfMembershipDraft's proofs parameter from cut 2, signs with the joiner's wallet, and offers QR + Mycelium delivery so the org-side acceptor can ingest through the existing self-membership-receive routing. Cut 3 pushed both SettingsScreen (823 lines) and HomeScreen (824 lines) over the file-size test's 800-line hard limit; two same-commit extractions resolve it cleanly: OrgDeclarationSection.tsx (encapsulates the org-creation form state machine — org name, org rules, join policy, busy, error) drops SettingsScreen 823→656; useOpenMemberRosterControls.ts (encapsulates the joinedMembers + pendingMembers useMemos + publishing flag + publish callback) drops HomeScreen 824→797 (three lines under the hard limit). Both extractions are clean component/hook boundaries rather than line-count surgery. Bundle budgets: three new explicit budgets (JoinPolicyPicker 3KB gz, JoinOrgModal 6KB gz, openMemberRoster helpers 2.5KB gz); three existing-chunk bumps (HomeScreen 18.5→19.5KB for the openMemberRoster static imports + JoinOrgModal-lazy declaration, SettingsScreen 10.5→11KB for the OrgDeclarationSection extraction landing in its static import graph, CSS 7.5→8KB for the new Tailwind utilities the picker sub-forms + the modal layout + the publish-roster amber chip introduced into the content scanner). All four gates green throughout: typecheck clean, eslint clean, 255 of 255 tests passing (no deltas — cut 3 is UI consumer of already-tested substrate), build OK with bundle budgets within limits.

why.text: Phase E4 cut 3 was named as the recommended first move by the prior letter, with the substrate (verifier + evaluator + builder + readers from cuts 1 and 2) fully landed and cut 3 being purely about exposing it to operator-visible surfaces. The chip-form question was explicitly pre-written by the prior carpenter — how wide to scope the cut — and per PFOR-019 + the prior letter's guidance carpenter surfaced it on session-start. Operator picked full cut 3 (all three threads in one session) which is structurally the right move because the three threads are interlocking parts of the same architectural claim: the JoinPolicyPicker is the producer side that declares the policy at org-creation time, the OrgIdentitySections Members view is the org-side consumer that surfaces accepted joiners + the publish-roster affordance, and the JoinOrgModal is the joiner-side consumer that builds + sends the self-membership envelope. Splitting them across sessions would have left the loop half-open with no operator-reachable end-to-end test of whether the substrate-to-UI bridge actually works. Landing all three together closes the Phase E arc end to end and confirms the cut 2 chip-form decision was answered correctly (the on-wire shape matched exactly what cut 3 needed; no surprises at integration time). The two extractions (OrgDeclarationSection + useOpenMemberRosterControls) were forced by the 800-line file-size test rather than chosen, but the extraction boundaries are clean — each piece has well-defined inputs/outputs and was never reused outside its consumer screen. Better to extract once at the boundary than to fight the line-count surgery on every subsequent addition.

This is real and is worth naming as documented carpenter doctrine when the operator next touches the standing orders.

confidence.uncertainty: Cut 3 is UI consumer of substrate that has full test coverage from prior sessions (evaluateJoinPolicy + verifyOpenJoinedMembership + buildSelfMembershipDraft + the proof readers + acceptedSelfMemberships + pendingSelfMemberships + publishOpenMemberRoster all tested via existing 255-test suite). The new UI components themselves are not component-tested because the vitest harness is pure logic — no React Testing Library in the toolchain. Adding component tests would require a toolchain extension (chip-worthy). The pure-function logic inside the new components — JoinPolicyPicker's per-kind validation, JoinOrgModal's describePolicy renderer + proof-candidate filters — mirrors patterns from buildAuthSubtree's contract or composes already-tested predicates. The vouch policy path in JoinOrgModal is structurally incomplete: the modal builds a joiner-signed envelope and surfaces a plain-prose notice that cosignatures from existing members must be collected, but does not orchestrate that collection itself. This is honest scope-down for cut 3 — the from-any-member-of-known-set picker shape is structurally different from the existing CosignRequestModal's from-named-eligible-list picker, and the design decision is chip-worthy. publishOfficialsRoster + publishOpenMemberRoster + receiveSelfMembership all hit anchorQueue.upsert which uses IndexedDB which jsdom does not back; tests exercise the pure builders + signed wallet.hold directly so the same envelope shape the production path emits is verified, but the full publish-pipeline storage round-trip stays unverified. Same uncertainty surface carried forward from prior sessions; not blocking.
